title: A Inheritance for the Verdict
premise: Hazel Kavanagh, a nonbinary night-shift dispatcher who solves missing persons cases from behind a radio console, takes on the disappearance of Marisol Vega, a court stenographer who vanished three weeks before her testimony in a corruption trial. The case seems routine until Hazel obtains Marisol's diary and finds entries dated after her disappearance—entries that describe Hazel's own investigation with unsettling accuracy. As the anniversary dinner approaches, where the city's legal elite will toast the trial's one-year mark, Hazel realizes the killer is someone inside the justice system, using the diary to taunt them personally. In the end, Hazel baits the killer into confessing on an open dispatch channel during the dinner itself, exposing a judge who erased witnesses to protect his legacy—and finally claiming a public identity they'd spent years hiding.
about_author: Gideon Almeida is a former emergency dispatcher turned novelist who writes mysteries set in the liminal hours when cities pretend to sleep. They live in a coastal town where fog rolls in early and everyone has at least one secret worth a chapter.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Hazel Kavanagh works the night shift at Citywide Taxi dispatch, solving small disappearances as a hobby no one knows about. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: competent solitude, the comfort of being unseen.

chapters.title: A Voice on Line Four
chapters.summary: Marisol Vega's sister calls dispatch asking for a cab that never arrived; Hazel recognizes the pattern of a staged vanishing. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: The Stenographer's Silence
chapters.summary: Hazel learns Marisol was transcribing testimony in the Halloran corruption trial before she disappeared. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the case grows teeth; stakes shift from personal to systemic.

chapters.title: Diary of a Missing Woman
chapters.summary: Marisol's sister surrenders the diary; its final entry describes fear of 'the man who writes the record.' POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: dread—the victim saw it coming.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Hazel discovers diary entries dated days after Marisol vanished, describing a dispatcher named Kavanagh by initials only. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: violation—the hunter realizes they are also hunted.

chapters.title: Nobody Knows My Name
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Hazel built their invisible life, changing names, avoiding records. POV: Hazel (past). Emotional beat: the cost of erasure, and why it was chosen.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Invitations circulate for the one-year gala marking the Halloran verdict; Hazel secures a catering-adjacent cover to attend. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: stepping out of the shadows, terrified but resolved.

chapters.title: Case File Ghosts
chapters.summary: Detective Imani Okafor catches Hazel probing police channels; instead of arresting them, she shares a detail the file never made public. POV: Imani. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people who trust nothing.

chapters.title: What the Transcript Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Hazel reconstructs Marisol's final workday through taxi logs, finding a repeated pickup address near the courthouse annex. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt returning, sharpened by fear.

chapters.title: The Man Who Writes the Record
chapters.summary: Hazel identifies three court officials with access to transcripts; each gets a quiet background check. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: methodical control masking rising panic.

chapters.title: Second Entry, Second Person
chapters.summary: A new diary page appears—slipped under Hazel's own door—describing their visit to the annex. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: terror made intimate; nowhere is safe.

chapters.title: Imani's Doubt
chapters.summary: Imani wonders if Hazel is fabricating evidence for attention; her lieutenant warns her off the Vega case. POV: Imani. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against institutional pressure.

chapters.title: The Sister's Version
chapters.summary: Lucía Vega reveals Marisol had been blackmailing someone to protect their family. POV: Lucía. Emotional beat: grief complicated by guilt over secrets kept.

chapters.title: Dispatch as Confessional
chapters.summary: Hazel uses old call recordings to trace Marisol's last cab ride; a driver remembers a judge's security detail. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the machinery of justice glimpsed from below.

chapters.title: Judge Aldous Wren
chapters.summary: Profile of Judge Wren, presiding over Halloran, whose legacy narrative depends on a clean verdict. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: chilling self-righteousness—he believes he is the good man.

chapters.title: An Invitation Accepted
chapters.summary: Hazel attends a pre-gala fundraiser under a borrowed name and watches Wren work a room. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: impostor syndrome colliding with righteous anger.

chapters.title: The Third Entry
chapters.summary: The diary predicts Hazel's fundraiser appearance verbatim; Hazel realizes the killer has access to their phone records. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: paranoia closing in like weather.

chapters.title: Inside the Annex
chapters.summary: Hazel breaks into the courthouse annex and finds Marisol's hidden duplicate transcript pages implicating Wren. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: triumph curdling—now they hold what killed her.

chapters.title: Loose Ends
chapters.summary: Wren's fixer, court clerk Dale Pruitt, begins quietly eliminating anyone who handled the transcript. POV: Pruitt. Emotional beat: banal evil, a man doing chores for power.

chapters.title: Imani Follows Hazel
chapters.summary: Imani tails Hazel to the annex, catches them fleeing, and must choose between procedure and partnership. POV: Imani. Emotional beat: the leap of faith.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One File
chapters.summary: Hazel shows Imani the post-disappearance diary entries; together they conclude the killer is writing fiction to frame someone else. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: shared purpose forged in the dark.

chapters.title: The Frame Takes Shape
chapters.summary: Police announce an arrest in the Vega case—an innocent taxi driver Hazel once vouched for. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: guilt detonating; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: With two days until the gala, Hazel maps Wren's security, schedule, and vanity. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing panic.

chapters.title: Pruitt's Ledger
chapters.summary: Imani pulls Pruitt's financials and finds payments routed through the same shell company as Halloran's bribes. POV: Imani. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by fear of what comes next.

chapters.title: Entry Nine
chapters.summary: The diary's ninth entry promises 'a toast at the anniversary' and names Hazel outright. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the trap is meant for them; they decide to walk in anyway.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Hazel and Imani rehearse the sting: an open dispatch channel, a planted transcript, a killer who can't resist correcting the record. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: fragile hope, hands almost steady.

chapters.title: What Hazel Is Afraid Of
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude: Hazel confronts why they hid—not shame, but the belief that being known means being controllable. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: tender, aching self-recognition.

chapters.title: Gala Night Begins
chapters.summary: Hazel enters the anniversary dinner wearing a server's jacket and the duplicate transcript in an inner pocket. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: heart pounding beneath a borrowed uniform.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Wren raises a glass to 'justice served'; Hazel slips the doctored transcript into the display binder beside him. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Correction on Channel Three
chapters.summary: Hazel reads the false transcript aloud on the open dispatch channel; Pruitt, unable to bear errors, corrects it live—confessing details only the killer would know. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Champagne and Handcuffs
chapters.summary: Imani arrests Pruitt in front of the city's elite; Wren's composure cracks as reporters arrive. POV: Imani. Emotional beat: public justice, long deferred, finally served hot.

chapters.title: The Man Behind the Clerk
chapters.summary: Pruitt, cornered, implicates Wren directly—but the diary entries were Pruitt's alone, written in Marisol's stolen voice. POV: Pruitt. Emotional beat: the puppeteer unmasked as another puppet.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Confronted with the annex transcript, Wren offers Hazel a bribe, then a threat; Hazel chooses neither. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: refusing to be bought or frightened—for the first time.

chapters.title: Recorded
chapters.summary: Hazel reveals Wren's threats were captured on the still-open channel; state investigators take him into custody. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: quiet thunder—the invisible witness heard at last.

chapters.title: Aftermath at Dawn
chapters.summary: News breaks; Lucía learns the truth of her sister's courage; the wrongly arrested driver goes free. POV: Lucía. Emotional beat: grief given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: The Real Diary
chapters.summary: Investigators recover Marisol's true final entries—hopeful, funny, planning to testify anyway. POV: Hazel reading. Emotional beat: meeting the victim as a person, not a puzzle.

chapters.title: Name, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: At the precinct, Hazel gives a full statement under their own chosen name, on the record, for the first time. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: identity claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Hazel returns to dispatch one last night, closes every open case on the board, and signs off. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: farewell to invisibility without regret.

chapters.title: The New Frequency
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Hazel launches an independent casework line with Imani as legal liaison; first caller is a scared kid with a missing brother. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: belonging found not in hiding but in service.

chapters.title: Anniversary, Revised
chapters.summary: One year on, Hazel, Imani, and Lucía share a private dinner on the gala's date—toasting the living instead of the verdict. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: peace earned, glass raised to those who stayed.
